In a two-flavor vacuum with CP-conserving mixing, CPT invariance strictly demands \(\mathcal{C}_ν(L) = \mathcal{C}_{\barν}(L)\), meaning any measured difference \(Δ\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{CPT}} \equiv \mathcal{C}_ν - \mathcal{C}_{\barν}\) serves as a clean, background-free witness of CPT violation. We derive exact, first-order analytical relations connecting this entanglement asymmetry to the standard probability asymmetry, the baseline reflection sums, and the long-baseline decoherence floor. To rigorously test the experimental viability of this framework, we perform extensive numerical simulations. We demonstrate that the framework projects stringent sensitivity limits on Standard-Model Extension (SME) parameters at DUNE-like densities, isolate a coordinate-independent CPT invariant, and show that the signal remains robust across realistic, variable Earth matter density profiles. Crucially, we identify a distinct 24-hour sidereal modulation of the entanglement asymmetry, providing a definitive temporal "smoking gun" to disentangle CPT violation from matter effects. Finally, we show that at PeV astrophysical energies, the reflection-sum mismatch scales up to \(10^{13}\) meters, opening a novel frontier for CPT tests beyond terrestrial experiments.

title: The Lives and Deaths of Red Supergiants
authors: Emma R. Beasor
abstract: Red supergiants (RSGs) represent a brief yet pivotal phase in the evolution of massive stars, encompassing the final stages of nuclear burning for many core-collapse supernova progenitors. Having expanded to 100 times larger than their main-sequence sizes, they occupy the cool, luminous extreme of the Hertzsprung--Russell diagram. Characterised by extended convective envelopes, complex and dynamic atmospheres, and, sometimes, substantial mass loss, RSGs play a critical role in shaping both their own evolutionary outcomes and the circumstellar environments into which they ultimately explode. Despite decades of study, fundamental aspects of RSG physics remain poorly constrained, including the mechanisms driving mass loss and the connection between observed RSG populations and the properties of Type II supernovae. Recent observational advances have transformed the field, revealing episodic mass-loss events, asymmetric circumstellar structures, and signs of rapid evolutionary change in individual objects. Alongside these advances, studies of Type II supernovae and their progenitors have raised important new questions about the final stages of massive star evolution, including the possibility of rapid changes in the years immediately preceding core collapse. Motivated by these developments, this review aims to describe our current understanding of how RSGs live and die, from their observed properties through to their role as supernova progenitors, and where that understanding remains incomplete.

title: 3D and 2D Radiation Non-ideal MHD modeling of the decay of FUor outbursts
authors: Yisheng Tu, Lee Hartmann, Zhaohuan Zhu, Conel M. O'D. Alexander, Fred J. Ciesla, Eric Rapp
abstract: FU Orionis (FUor) outbursts are high-accretion events in protoplanetary disks thought to be driven by the magnetorotational instability (MRI). Although these outbursts span a wide range of observed durations and can thermally process and potentially transport disk material, the physical processes governing their decay remain poorly understood. We present a three-dimensional radiative non-ideal magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulation of the decay of an MRI-driven FUor outburst, complemented by a suite of two-dimensional models that explore its dependence on disk properties. During the decay, rings and gaps form naturally within the inner disk. Magnetic flux preferentially concentrates in the gaps, while the rings remain comparatively weakly magnetized. We show that MRI-active rings act as ``magnetic dams,'' confining magnetic flux within adjacent gaps. As the rings cool below the MRI activation temperature, non-ideal MHD effects decouple the gas from the magnetic field, allowing the trapped flux to diffuse outward. This outward diffusion can sometimes transiently reactivate MRI in neighboring rings, producing localized reheating events that we term ``Reactivation.'' By comparing otherwise identical two- and three-dimensional simulations, we find that MRI heating is systematically less efficient in two dimensions, leading to outburst durations shorter by a factor of $\sim3$--4. Our model suite further shows that the decay timescale depends primarily on the disk surface density and distance from the central star, with only a weak dependence on the magnetic field strength. We further derive an empirical relation linking the outburst duration to these quantities.

title: ExplicitIR: Explicit Spatial Policy Fields for All-in-One Image Restoration
authors: Dezhi Zhang, Shangrong Yang, Yudong Liang, Wenjian Wang
abstract: All-in-one image restoration aims to recover clean images blindly from inputs with various degradation types and levels using a single model. However, the adaptation policy in most existing methods remains implicitly encoded in feature representations, leaving the restoration decision neither explicitly represented nor independently controllable. Since real-world degradations vary spatially, applying uniform updates across the entire image leads to over-smoothing of clean areas and under-correction of localized degradations. To address these limitations, we present ExplicitIR, which represents the restoration policy as two explicit per-pixel fields: Budget, which determines where and how strongly to update, and Style, which selects between narrow and wide context windows. Specifically, ExplicitIR incorporates a Spatial Policy Estimator (SPE) to predict these fields, explicitly representing the restoration policy and capturing spatially-varying degradations, which are then applied by Policy-Adaptive Decoder Blocks (PADB) through adaptive fusion of narrow- and wide-window responses, enabling independent control and precise local modulation. This design enables spatially-adaptive restoration in a single forward pass, without requiring task labels, prompts, or test-time degradation estimators. Extensive experiments on three-task and five-task benchmarks demonstrate that ExplicitIR achieves performance competitive with the strongest all-in-one baselines.

title: Cross-cultural Adaptation of Recipes for Low-Resource Languages: A Benchmark and Multilingual Culinary Lexicon for Hausa, Yorùbá, and Igbo
authors: Nuhu Ibrahim, Maryam Abdulazeez, Fatsuma Jauro, Salisu Aliyu, Robert Stevens, Riza Batista-Navarro
abstract: Recent multilingual large language models (LLMs) have improved machine translation, yet culturally adaptive translation for low-resource languages (LRLs) remains underexplored. This is particularly challenging for recipes, where ingredients, cooking tools, measurements, and procedures may require adaptation to the target cultural context. In this work, we introduce ReciLoReL, a benchmark of 600 expert-translated and culturally adapted recipes across Yorùbá, Hausa, and Igbo (three of the most prominent languages in Nigeria), and ReciLex, a multilingual culinary lexicon containing approximately 15,000 translated entities across ten recipe entity categories, including ingredients, tools, chef actions, state of tools, and durations. We evaluate state-of-the-art multilingual LLMs for English-to-LRL recipe translation under zero-shot and few-shot settings and investigate whether augmenting LLMs with ReciLex improves culturally adaptive recipe translation without requiring large target-language recipe corpora for training or fine-tuning. Beyond conventional reference-based translation evaluation using BLEU, chrF, and TER, we introduce five criteria for evaluating cultural adaptation, adapted from established cross-cultural adaptation methods. Across the selected LLMs and languages, ReciLex improves average BLEU from 13.57 to 14.51 and chrF from 37.89 to 38.74, while reducing TER from 77.14 to 75.12. Human evaluation further shows improvements ranging from 0.11 to 0.36 points across the five cultural adaptation evaluation criteria on a five-point scale. Overall, our work provides new resources, evaluation criteria, and empirical evaluation for studying culturally adaptive recipe translation in low-resource settings.

title: The Minimal Background Period for Infinitely Many Spectral Gaps in Anderson-Bernoulli Models
authors: Cong Chen, Yong Li
abstract: We prove that three is the smallest background period for which a one-dimensional discrete Anderson-Bernoulli operator can have infinitely many gaps in its almost-sure spectrum. For an explicit period-three background and coupling, we construct infinitely many bounded gaps accumulating from the right at a spectral energy, for every nondegenerate Bernoulli law. This property persists on an open set of background and coupling parameters. The proof combines a transverse heteroclinic connection and invariant multicones with spectral points from periodic realizations. A strict geometric window permits integer scale matching, and the required parameter inequalities are verified by exact rational arithmetic.

title: On the velocity range limitation of DBSCAN for event-based particle tracking and a proposed solution
authors: Nicolas Lanchon, Charlotte Vienney, Samuel Bera, Cheng Wang, Adam Cheminet, Nicolas Plihon, Romain Volk, Mickaël Bourgoin, Bérengère Dubrulle
abstract: Event-based cameras offer new opportunities for particle tracking in fluid mechanics by providing asynchronous, sparse measurements with high temporal resolution and no fixed acquisition frequency. Processing such data requires algorithms capable of fully exploiting these distinctive features. A natural first approach to perform particle tracking on event-based data is to apply a clustering algorithm, in particular DBSCAN, as it does not require specifying the number of clusters a priori. In this paper, we show, using a simplified synthetic two-particle system, that this classical algorithm is severely limited in terms of the accessible velocity range vmax/vmin. To address this limitation, and to take advantage of the absence of a fixed acquisition frequency in event-based cameras, we propose a new two-dimensional, two-component (2D2C) particle-tracking algorithm based on clustering. The method relies on a recursive application of DBSCAN with multiple temporal normalizations, retaining only clusters that satisfy a set of validation criteria. A key feature of the proposed algorithm is that it does not assume any characteristic time scale or typical velocity. The algorithm is evaluated on realistic synthetic datasets generated from numerical simulations of turbulent flows, and the influence of key parameters is systematically investigated. Particular attention is given to the definition of evaluation metrics adapted to clusters of events for particle tracking. Finally, the proposed algorithm is applied to experimental data acquired in a turbulent flow generated by a von

title: TANGO: Real-World Unregistered RGB-Guided Hyperspectral Super-Resolution with Two-Camera Acquisitions
authors: Matteo Kolyszko, Marco Buzzelli, Simone Bianco, Raimondo Schettini
abstract: Unregistered hyperspectral image super-resolution aims to recover a high-resolution HSI from a low-resolution hyperspectral observation and an unregistered high-resolution RGB reference. Although recent methods have begun to address the geometric misalignment between the two modalities, their evaluation is still constrained by the lack of a large-scale public benchmark based on real two-camera RGB--HSI acquisitions with a high-resolution HSI reference. To address this gap, we introduce DUET, the first large-scale public dataset for unregistered RGB-guided hyperspectral super-resolution, comprising 403 indoor and outdoor scenes captured with two separate RGB and hyperspectral cameras. We further propose TANGO (Two-camera AligNment with Gated Occlusions), which first compensates for the dominant cross-camera displacement through end-to-end global alignment and then refines the remaining inconsistencies with a coarse-to-fine local feature alignment. A learned gating mechanism further attenuates the RGB guidance where the two views cannot be consistently matched. Experimental results show that TANGO achieves state-of-the-art performance on both DUET and REAL across all evaluated scale factors, outperforming the strongest competitor on DUET by up to 2.29 dB in PSNR while requiring 2.5$\times$ fewer FLOPs. The code and dataset will be available at https://github.com/FagiolottoConSombrero/TANGO-DUET

title: Hausdorff reflections and obstruction ideals for filter topologies on MV-algebras
authors: Yanyan Dong, Bin Pang, Yi Shi
abstract: MV-algebras arise in many-valued logic and are closely related to lattice-ordered groups. We characterize Hausdorff separation in filter topologies through their associated ideals. For every proper lattice filter, $T_0$, $T_1$ and $T_2$ are equivalent, and the zero-neighborhood ideal determines a canonical Hausdorff reflection. For a radius filter satisfying a refinement condition, the filter topology agrees with the ambient subspace topology exactly when every radius is a weak order unit. This answers a question of Luan, Zhao and Yang without requiring divisibility of the representing group. These results reveal two successive algebraic obstructions: a polar obstruction controlling compatibility with the ambient topology, followed by a relative infinitesimal obstruction controlling the residual failure of Hausdorff separation. For a unital lattice-ordered subring of $C(X,\mathbb R)$, where $X$ is compact Hausdorff and the unit is $\mathbf1$, the associated exact sequence admits a positive additive section exactly when the relative infinitesimal ideal vanishes.

title: Another Variant of the Neoclassical Inequality
authors: Stefan Gerhold
abstract: The neoclassical inequality is an inequality related to the binomial theorem, involving fractional powers. It naturally gives rise to four other similar inequalities, by varying the inequality sign and the range of the fractional parameter. Three of these statements are known, and the remaining one was conjectured in the literature, based on numerical evidence. It is proved in the present note. The method we use yields short proofs for two of the known related inequalities.

title: Visibility Graph Representations of Word Embeddings for Text Classification
authors: Elif Dorukbaşı, İlker Türker
abstract: Text classifiers depend on representations that expose the distinctions between classes in a form the learning model can use, and a restricted vocabulary changes which representation is most effective. This paper studies natural visibility graphs as an intermediate representation for news topic classification under controlled vocabulary budgets. Word embeddings are averaged into a fixed-length document vector, the vector is read as an ordered numerical series, and its natural visibility graph is passed to a classifier either as an ordered node-degree vector or as an adjacency matrix. On the four-class AG News benchmark, chi-square selection retains 100 to 1,500 words, and the graph inputs are compared with direct embedding-based representations from continuous bag-of-words, skip-gram, GloVe, FastText and BERT. With a fully connected classifier, the degree representation is the most accurate configuration from 700 selected words onward; it reaches its highest accuracy of 91.24% at 1,000 words and exceeds the BERT-based baseline by 0.29 percentage points at 1,500 words. In a separate convolutional comparison, the adjacency input reaches 86.16% at 1,000 words, against 83.12% for the strongest static embedding. The results indicate that visibility-derived features can be competitive once the selected vocabulary provides adequate coverage. We discuss the roles of graph compression, coordinate ordering and classifier choice, and the controls needed to establish the reliability of the small differences observed.

title: Classification of Tissues on MALDI-MSI Image Modality for Pancreatic Cancer Studies
authors: Abubakar Qahir, Jenny Benois-Pineau, Victoria Bourgeais, Fabien Baldacci, Sandrine Dabernat, Nicolas Desbenoit, Mélanie Moreau, Mehdi Boubaddi, Marion Marty
abstract: Mass Spectrometry Imaging (MSI) spatially maps molecular distributions in tissue sections. Despite the availability of preprocessing tools for MSI data, building end-to-end workflows suitable for deep learning remains challenging. We have developed a fully automated pipeline for transformation of raw Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization Mass Spectrometry imaging (MALDI-MSI) data into deep-learning-ready image patches for binary pancreatic tissue classification (tumoral vs non-tumoral) and built individual models for recognition of tumoral regions in spectral images. Images resulting from the proposed pipeline and from reference interactive workflow are very close in terms of image quality metric mean squared error (MSE). The proposed pipeline computational time is of 20 min in average compared to a full working day of the reference interactive workflow. The models achieved 0.94 accuracy on high-resolution spectra and a mean accuracy of 0.59 on lower-resolution spectra.

title: Convection--diffusion equations with non-integrable initial data
authors: Nicola De Nitti, Liviu I. Ignat, Fernando Quirós
abstract: We characterize the long-time behaviour of solutions to the convection--diffusion equation $u_t-u_{xx}+(|u|^{q-1}u)_x=0$, $q>1$, with initial data behaving like a non-integrable power at infinity, $|x|^γu_0(x)\to k_\pm$ as $x\to\pm\infty$, $0<γ\le1$. The decay rate in time and the asymptotic profile depend on the strength of convection as compared to the size of the solution at infinity, leading either to a convective behaviour or to a diffusive one. When the nonlinear convection dominates, we observe an enhanced dissipation effect: the decay rate in time is faster than for the purely diffusive equation with the same initial datum. For $0<γ<1$ we obtain the limit self-similar profile, which, in the convective regime, has one shock, or two when $k_+k_-<0$ and $|k_+|>\eps(γ,q)|k_-|$, where $\eps(γ,q)\in(0,1)$ is an explicit threshold. For $γ=1$ logarithmic corrections appear, and the limit is a multiple of the heat kernel if $q>2$ and an $N$-wave if $1<q\le2$. The convergence takes place in the spaces to which the datum belongs, and not only on expanding sets. The main new ingredients are an Oleĭnik type estimate of Hölder type valid for $q\geq 2$ and a far-field estimate, uniform in time, showing that beyond the self-similar region the solution is still described by its own datum.

title: Let Samples Sing in Chorus: Mitigating Spurious Correlations via Cross-view Consensus
authors: Weiwei Li, Junzhuo Liu, Tong Chu, Hengfu Yu, Yinjie Lei, Wen Li
abstract: Deep models often rely on spurious correlations that fail on underrepresented groups. Existing methods either correct human-specified bias attributes or infer unknown biases from the learned representation space. However, annotated attributes may differ from the shortcuts actually used by a model, while a single representation provides incomplete and potentially noisy evidence. Our key insight is that a bias obscured in one feature space may be clearer in another. In this work, we propose CHORD (Cross-view Harmonic Outlier Reversal for Debiasing), a multi-view framework that allows samples to "sing in chorus" across diverse representation spaces to achieve robust cross-view consensus. CHORD aggregates aggregates within-class partitions in each view, which is a proxy for specifying candidate biases, to debias the target representation and classifier without bias supervision. Experiments on seven benchmarks across vision, language, speech, and medical imaging show consistent improvements in worst-group accuracy. Code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/davelee-uestc/chord_debiasing_public .

title: VQkit: A Unified and Extensible Framework for VASP and Quantum ESPRESSO Pre- and Post-Processing
authors: Rajkamal Anand, Seunghwan Kwon, Gun Jin Yun
abstract: VQkit is a Python-based computational toolkit developed to streamline the pre- and post-processing of density functional theory calculations performed using Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP) and Quantum ESPRESSO (QE). The framework employs a unified representation of lattice vectors, atomic coordinates, chemical species, and positional constraints, enabling cross-code structure conversion, geometry manipulation, crystallographic reconstruction, and code-specific input generation. Its pre-processing capabilities include symmetry-dependent reciprocal-space path generation, atomic constraints, and automated preparation of simulation inputs. The post-processing framework provides calculation convergence inspection, extraction of total energies and Fermi levels, electronic band-structure and density-of-states analysis, orbital-resolved electronic-structure processing, charge-density analysis, and evaluation of application-specific materials properties. The computational implementation is evaluated through elastic-property benchmarks for HfC, ZrC, ZrO2, Ti, and diamond, showing close agreement between VQkit and VASPKIT for VASP-based calculations, with differences observed in the corresponding QE results. By integrating cross-code interoperability, automated simulation preparation, standardized post-processing, and quantitative property evaluation within a common computational environment, VQkit reduces workflow fragmentation and facilitates consistent pre- and post-processing of first-principles calculations.

title: A Unifying Metatheorem on Weak-Memory Robustness
authors: Giovanna Kobus Conrado, Stephan Spengler, Mohamed Faouzi Atig, Andreas Pavlogiannis
abstract: Memory models specify the behaviors that concurrent programs may exhibit under compiler and hardware optimizations, which often deviate from Sequential Consistency (SC). Robustness is the property of a program P not exhibiting any weak behaviors when executing under a weak memory model MM, compared to SC. As such, the algorithmic problem of deciding whether $P$ is robust against MM has been studied extensively, and has been repeatedly shown to be in PSPACE for many memory models, such as TSO, PSO, and Release/Acquire. However, each model has required its own, dedicated proof, raising the natural question of whether robustness admits a unifying treatment across memory models. In this work, we answer this question affirmatively for a broad class of memory models definable in Kleene Algebra with Tests (KAT). We prove that robustness against any prefix-closed, KAT-definable memory model is in PSPACE. This metatheorem recovers nearly all prior PSPACE robustness results, and establishes PSPACE membership for several new models, including the full RC11 and the OCaml memory model. We have further formalized the correctness of our approach in Lean. On the other hand, we prove that robustness against the KAT-definable Relaxed model is undecidable, and thus prefix-closedness cannot be dropped, in general. Finally, we implement our algorithm in a prototype tool RoboKAT, and demonstrate its flexibility by checking robustness against nine memory models, several of which are not handled by prior work.

title: Domain walls of a spin-chirality ferroelectric as tunable quantum particles
authors: Aleksandr Buzdakov, Atharva Hingane, Sergey Artyukhin
abstract: In frustrated spin chains with competing nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor exchange, the vector spin chirality sets the electric polarization, so a ferroelectric domain wall is a domain wall of the chirality. The semiclassical picture suggests nonlocal switching dynamics due to topological constraints on the spins, but little is known about such domain walls in a quantum spin chain. Using density-matrix renormalization group calculations for a frustrated spin-1/2 XXZ chain in which a bond alternation $δ$ opens a spin gap, we show that the wall then becomes a quantum particle. In a finite chain, it has the energy levels and wave functions of a particle in a box, and it moves under an electric field as a particle under a constant force does. In the infinite chain, its mass grows by more than two orders of magnitude as $δ$ decreases and diverges at $δ^*\approx0.012$, where the bottom of its band becomes flat; below $δ^*$ the band has two degenerate minima away from its center. The large mass results from a near cancellation of in-plane and out-of-plane exchange energies.

title: The Between-Round Decision in Autonomous Research: An LLM Controller That Reads the Whole Trajectory
authors: Caoxin Wang, Shengkai Gan, Xiang Hu, Lili Pan
abstract: Executing an idea often changes how promising it looks, so the next step in autonomous research should rest on results, not on proposals. After each round of experiments, the system must decide whether to refine the best solution or start a new direction, which solution to build from, and what goal to set. We call this the between-round decision. Existing systems wrap it in machinery such as rules, scores, search trees, and schedules; where an LLM makes it, what the LLM needs to read is left open. We ask whether an LLM can make this decision from accumulated evidence, without a search structure around it, and how much of that evidence it needs to read. We present BRED (Between-Round Evidence-based Decision), an LLM-based controller that maintains the best verified solution so far (the Champion) and a log of past rounds, and makes one decision per round. On three widely used research-agent benchmark tasks, BRED improves on the task baselines by 4.80% in MAE on ETTh1 (to 0.4172) and by 3.44 and 3.43 points of accuracy on SST-2 (to 95.07%) and CIFAR-100 (to 84.63%), ahead of the published results. When the controller does not read the accumulated evidence, the same loop gains less: with no history it reaches 0.4299 on ETTh1 and 83.71% on CIFAR-100, whereas the full controller's MAE is 2.95% lower and its accuracy 0.92 points higher. On a new task, speech-based depression detection under a leakage-free protocol, it reaches a macro-F1 of 0.6164 on seeds held out from selection, 5.5 points above its baseline and 4.0 above the strongest published system. Code is available at https://github.com/learninginvision/BRED.

title: Risk Density RRT$^*$: Planning in the Space of Probability
authors: Lorenzo Paiola, Giorgio Grioli, Antonio Bicchi
abstract: Planning under uncertainty is a fundamental problem in robotics. While much of the literature seeks minimum-cost paths subject to probabilistic constraints, this paper instead considers collision probability, or risk classically defined as probability times severity, directly as the planning objective. We propose Risk Density RRT$^*$ (RD-RRT$^*$), an extension of RRT$^*$ for high-level planning in environments with deterministic and uncertain obstacles. RD-RRT$^*$ builds on Risk Density, a functional that evaluates a continuous path as a whole and provides a tractable approximation of its collision probability. The framework also supports severity-weighted risk and a hybrid variant that adds a path-length penalty, balancing risk and geometric efficiency while regularizing exploration in low-density regions. We validate the method across a wide range of scenarios. The results show that RD-RRT$^*$ consistently finds paths with lower estimated collision probability by optimizing a global risk-based objective. We further demonstrate the fidelity of the underlying approximation through Monte Carlo simulations. Finally, we discuss how the topological structure induced by Risk Density may provide a useful representation of the environment and offer insights into risk-aware planning.

title: OmniTongue: A Comprehensive MLLM Benchmark for Automated Tongue Diagnosis in Traditional Chinese Medicine
authors: Liuyi Xu, Yun Guo, Shusheng Li, Xuewen Zhang, Yining Qian, An-Yang Lu
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have excelled in Western medical imaging, yet their potential in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) tongue diagnosis remains systematically unevaluated. Tongue diagnosis requires sophisticated global and local perception, serving as a rigorous touchstone for assessing the visual understanding depth of MLLMs. However, existing datasets are limited by single dimensions, coarse granularity, and ambiguous labels, hindering the evaluation of authentic clinical capabilities. To bridge this gap, we introduce OmniTongue, the first comprehensive, fine-grained Visual Question Answering benchmark for TCM tongue diagnosis. This benchmark integrates 1,351 expert-validated images and 21,616 instruction pairs. Its core design features 16 clinical dimensions for multidimensional evaluation, region-specific annotations for pathological localization, and 66 fine-grained labels for precise diagnostic representation. Extensive evaluations of existing MLLMs reveal significant performance gaps, demonstrating that medical-specific models lack domain advantages, while universally poor Macro-F1 scores expose a reliance on statistical shortcuts rather than genuine understanding of tongue pathology. These findings not only highlight the current limitations of MLLMs in interpreting regional medical features but also underscore OmniTongue's significance for developing robust automated tongue diagnosis models. The code and dataset will be made publicly available in a future release.

title: Inflation with an Exponential Power-Law Potential:Analytical Slow-Roll Relations, Branch Dynamics, and Conditional Reheating Matching
authors: Feyzollah Younesizadeh, Younes Younesizadeh, Wen-Xiang Chen
abstract: We study canonical single-field inflation driven by the potential $V(φ)=M^4\exp(φ/M_{\rm Pl})(1+kφ/M_{\rm Pl})^{-1/k}$ with $k<0$. We retain the canonical Einstein--scalar action and derive analytical relations within the slow-roll approximation. Expressing the local spectra through the logarithmic slope $A=kx/(1+kx)$, with $x=φ/M_{\rm Pl}$, yields an endpoint-independent consistency relation among the scalar tilt, tensor ratio, and running at their stated approximation orders. On the negative-field branch, an exact phase-space argument shows that an initially downhill, inflationary hilltop trajectory cannot end inflation within the bare single-field model. We specify the endpoint as a phenomenological input and use a Lambert-$W$ solution of the slow-roll e-fold integral. Tables and figures illustrate the fixed choice $x_e=-2$ and must be interpreted conditionally on a completion that implements this endpoint and preserves the adiabatic spectrum. The reheating-matching relation uses explicit scale and thermal conventions and imposes both endpoint energy bounds and nonnegative reheating duration. The observational comparison uses published marginalized intervals rather than reconstructed joint posteriors. These results establish local analytical structure and conditional numerical benchmarks. A complete exit mechanism, a unique reheating equation of state, and precision spectral predictions remain unestablished.

title: Back to Mel: Learning to Bridge Fidelity and Perception in Generative Speech Enhancement
authors: Andong Li, Kun Zhou, Xiaodong Li, Chengshi Zheng
abstract: Recent generative techniques have facilitated the rapid proliferation of speech enhancement approaches built upon learnable compact latent representations and large generative backbones. Nevertheless, it remains inherently challenging to balance between acoustic fidelity, perceptual quality, and processing efficiency. In this paper, we revisit the Mel spectrum as a structured acoustic representation and propose BAME, a flow-matching-based framework that exploits the complementary priors for generative speech enhancement task. First, leveraging the explicit hierarchical frequency distribution of Mel spectrum, we elaborately devise a subband-aware Transformer (SaT) for efficient generative modeling. Using only 2.9% of the parameters, the proposed SaT achieves superior enhancement performance compared with a 331 M DiT backbone. Second, motivated by range-null decomposition theory of Mel filtering in the magnitude-spectral domain, we introduce a phase-aware neural vocoder that incorporates degraded-phase prior, together with a quality-guided dual-phase strategy to adaptively mitigate the effects of unreliable phase information. Third, we devise a simple yet effective one-step fidelity-perception alignment strategy that fine-tunes the flow model with complementary constraints from fidelity and perception domains. Extensive experiments are conducted on DNS-Challenge, EARS, GSR, and URGENT benchmarks, and both objective and subjective results demonstrate promising performance on various intrusive and non-intrusive evaluation metrics. These results further advocate the potential of exploiting structured acoustic representations for reliable and efficient generative speech enhancement. Audio samples and codes are available at https://github.com/AndongLi-speech/BAME.

title: Hardness and Inapproximability of the Covering Radius for LDPC Codes
authors: Massimo Battaglioni, Fabrizio Marinelli
abstract: Given a binary parity-check matrix $H$ and an integer $r$, the covering-radius decision problem asks whether every attainable syndrome can be represented by an error vector of Hamming weight at most $r$. We study this problem for sparse parity-check matrices with bounded row and column weights. Using a bounded-occurrence quantified-SAT reduction, we prove that the problem is $Π_2^{\mathrm P}$-complete for matrices with maximum row and column weight three, and remains $Π_2^{\mathrm P}$-hard under a constant multiplicative gap. Starting from Vertex Cover on 3-regular graphs, we also obtain an explicit NP-hard approximation factor under the same weight constraints. We remark that weight three is the exact threshold for hardness: if either the maximum row weight or the maximum column weight is at most two, the covering radius can be computed in polynomial time.

title: EvoSkill-S1: Evolving Reusable Skills with Genetic-Inspired Operators
authors: Yujun Wang, Jiqiang Li, Yinuo Lu, Jinhe Bi, Aniri, Wenxuan Ye, Boliang Liu, Sikuan Yan, Shuning Wang, Xuebing Zhou, S{ö}ren Pirk, Hinrich Sch{ü}tze, Yunpu Ma
abstract: Reusable skills allow language-model agents to accumulate and reuse problem-solving experience. However, most existing methods improve a skill bank only indirectly through rollout-driven accumulation and heuristic reflection, often resulting in shallow and weakly controlled updates. We present EvoSkill-S1, an RL-driven framework that instead treats reusable skills themselves as the direct objects of evolution. Given hard-negative failures, EvoSkill-S1 selects parent skills and transforms them into candidate child skills through five genetic-inspired operators: revision, cross-revision, mutation, dual-reflection, and crossover. Downstream task rewards train the skill evolver to generate more effective child skills, while evaluator-guided write-back selectively retains beneficial updates. Complementary Skill Bank Fusion consolidates operator-specific banks to exploit their distinct recovery patterns, while a Procedural Skill Interface supports transfer to unseen problems. Across all reported math and code benchmarks, EvoSkill-S1 improves the corresponding initialized skill banks under both Qwen and GPT-family solvers, with relative gains of up to 12.39%. Compared with the strongest external baseline without direct skill evolution, the largest relative improvement reaches 20.39%.

title: A variational multiscale rotational pressure-correction method for incompressible flows with open boundaries
authors: Peishuo Wu, Chi Zhu
abstract: Rotational pressure correction improves pressure accuracy near open boundaries in incompressible flow simulations, but equal-order finite element discretizations can still develop spurious pressure oscillations. We develop a residual-based variational multiscale rotational pressure-correction scheme (RPCS-VMS) that stabilizes both the pressure-increment and pressure-recovery equations. By constructing stage-specific momentum residuals using a common intermediate-velocity acceleration, the scheme retains four sequential linear solves per time step. For a reduced BDF1 Oseen model with frozen stabilization coefficients, we establish augmented-energy decay and a conditional bound on the pressure gradient. Manufactured-solution tests demonstrate suppression of pressure oscillations at small time steps and reduced near-boundary pressure errors. With \(P_1/P_1\) and \(Q_1/Q_1\) elements, the observed spatial \(L^2\) convergence rates are 2 for velocity and approximately \(1.5\) for pressure, while first- and second-order backward differentiation formulas attain their expected temporal orders. Branched-pipe and two- and three-dimensional cylinder benchmarks assess outlet flow partitioning, transient forces, and pressure differences, with results agreeing closely with reference solutions. In the three-dimensional cylinder test, RPCS-VMS achieves a 2.41-fold wall-time speedup over the tested monolithic VMS solver.

title: Constructions of reversible linear and DNA codes through $T_{D,g}^n-$set and $(n_1,c_1|n_2,c_2)-$right polycyclic codes
authors: Avanish Kumar Chaturvedi, Satyadeep Pandey
abstract: In this paper we give a construction technique of $T_{D,g}^n-$set for reversible linear codes and reversible DNA codes with their code parameters. This technique yields many reversible MDS codes which significantly improves the $T^n-$set construction by Oztas et.al. in terms of obtained code parameters. Concatenation-based constructions are presented for reversible linear codes satisfying self-duality and linear complementary dual (LCD) conditions, giving necessary and sufficient condition for desired dual properties. We introduce a new notion of $(n_1,c_1|n_2,c_2)-$ right polycyclic codes. Also, a new construction technique is developed to obtain reversible linear $(n_1,c_1|n_2,c_2)-$ right polycyclic codes with good parameters (MDS codes) over any finite commutative rings.

title: Evolution Under Fire: Evolving Agent Safety Harnesses with Adaptive Injection Stressors
authors: Yujun Wang, Yilun Liu, Jinhe Bi, Krishna Kanth Nakka, Xuebing Zhou, Hinrich Sch{ü}tze, Yunpu Ma
abstract: Tool-using language-model agents must act on information from untrusted emails, webpages, and documents. This creates a central security challenge: malicious instructions and legitimate task directives can arrive through the same interaction channel. Existing defenses are largely hand-designed and static, making further improvements dependent on repeated manual redesign. We introduce Evolution Under Fire, a staged framework that couples safety-harness evolution with adaptive stressor evolution. Utility-constrained, Pareto-scheduled tree search evolves complete executable safety harnesses from execution evidence while keeping the task model, benchmark, tools, and evaluator fixed. Adaptive stressor evolution then discovers utility-preserving attacks that guide a subsequent stage of harness evolution. On AgentDyn with GPT-4o-mini, an evolved harness reduces attack success from 50.4% to 3.0%, improves clean and attacked utility over the initial harness, and offers a stronger security-utility trade-off than reproduced defenses. On Agent-SafetyBench with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, harness evolution reduces attack success from 82.6% to 62.0% while retaining helpfulness and runtime validity. Evolved harnesses also transfer without further evolution to Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, reducing attack success from 32.1% to 0.9% while improving attacked-task utility.

title: Do LLMs Understand Network Traces? A Comparative Study of Reasoning over Raw and Filtered Traffic Data
authors: Irene Gosálvez-White, Roberto Magán-Carrión, Carlota de la Vega-Soriano, Pedro García-Teodoro
abstract: The effective delivery and monitoring of ICT services rely heavily on network traffic analysis. However, interpreting complex packet captures remains a challenging task that requires substantial technical expertise. Large language models (LLMs) offer promising opportunities to automate network traffic in- vestigation, yet their reliability in packet-level field extraction and flow-level sequence reconstruction remains an open research question. This study proposes a reproducible, question-answering- based evaluation methodology to assess the capabilities of LLMs in network trace analysis. Using real-world benign traffic from the CICIDS2017 dataset, we evaluate multiple models against a human-generated ground truth, comparing their performance on raw textual traffic dumps and protocol-filtered representations. Model responses are assessed through an automated LLM- as-a-judge pipeline, validated against human evaluations. The results demonstrate that protocol filtering significantly reduces prompt overhead while improving answer accuracy by reducing incorrect responses. These findings highlight the importance of protocol-aware traffic filtering as an effective optimization for improving the efficiency and reliability of LLM-assisted network management.

title: Targeted material doping to enable the formation and coherent propagation of Laser Induced Periodic Surface Structures (LIPSS): the ZnO paradigm
authors: Gonzalo Gomez-Munoz, Rocio Ariza, Juan Francisco Ramos-Justicia, Fatima Cabello Pardos, Antonio Pablo Pérez-Marín, Jose Gonzalo, Belén Sotillo, Binbing Xia, Paloma Fernandez, Javier Solis
abstract: This work explores how the initial free carrier density governs the formation and coherent propagation of Low Spatial Frequency Laser-Induced Periodic Surface Structures (LSF-LIPSS). As a paradigm we have analyzed the behavior of ad-hoc-doped ZnO films. ZnO is a multifunctional Transparent Conducting Oxide (TCO) with many scientific and technologic uses including applications in biomedicine, photonics, sensing or photocatalysis. Many of them would benefit from the use of large area, electrically anisotropic surfaces. By introducing small amounts of Yb3+ as donor dopant in ZnO films grown by Pulse Laser Deposition (PLD), we have substantially improved its carrier density at room temperature (RT) and its electrical conductivity while preserving the functional properties of pure ZnO. For RT carrier densities ne > 1019 cm-3, coherent propagation of LSF-LIPSS has been successfully achieved upon irradiation with 350 fs laser pulses at 1030 nm at high repetition rate (500 kHz) and for laser scanning speeds well above 1 m/s. However, the ablation mechanism (ZnO sublimation at the LIPSS valleys) and the large melting temperature of ZnO, make the thermal conductivity of the substrate, the film thickness and the irradiation pulse duration to play a crucial role in determining the morphology of the LSF-LIPPS propagated over large areas, especially in avoiding film cracking. The results achieved upon optimization fully confirm the role of free carrier density in the large-scale propagation of high quality LSF-LIPSS in doped ZnO and enable using these structures to easily generate large electrical anisotropies over macroscopic regions with conductivities along the LIPSS several times larger than transversally.

title: Planet Formation in a Warped Disc: Gravitational Instability and Misaligned Infall
authors: Sahl Rowther, Josh Calcino, Richard Alexander
abstract: We perform three-dimensional smoothed particle hydrodynamics simulations to investigate the impact of misaligned infall on a gravitationally unstable protoplanetary disc. The interaction between the disc and the infalling gas does not occur uniformly across all radii. As infall impacts the outer disc first, the outer disc experiences stronger torques than the inner disc, resulting in a warped disc where the angular momentum vector of the disc varies with radius. The surrounding infalling gas reprocesses stellar irradiation and re-emits it back towards the disc, resulting in a warmer disc. The higher temperatures cause the disc to become more gravitationally stable resulting in weaker spiral arms. However, over time, infall also continuously increases the disc mass, gradually altering the local conditions and strengthening gravitational instabilities despite the azimuthally averaged Toomre $Q$ indicating that the disc is stable against gravitational instability. Eventually, one of the spiral arms fragments, forming a giant planet by gravitational instability in a disc warped by misaligned infall. Hence, the impact of infall on gravitational instability in general will vary depending on the infall and disc properties due to the balance between the stabilising and destabilising effects. We also find that infall alters the expected signatures of gravitationally unstable discs by introducing asymmetries in scattered-light, continuum, and molecular line emission.

title: Non-integrability of open strings via Pohlmeyer reduction
authors: Divania Carelse, Laila Tribelhorn, Konstantinos Zoubos
abstract: We study integrable and non-integrable boundary conditions for classical strings from the point of view of Pohlmeyer reduction. We first consider the integrable case of strings ending on Y=0 non-maximal giant gravitons. Pohlmeyer reduction of such strings leads to a sine-Gordon model, for which a criterion for boundary integrability was provided by Ghoshal and Zamolodchikov. We confirm that the Pohlmeyer field satisfies this condition. We then turn to the main focus of our work, which is open strings on AdS3. By evaluating the Ghoshal-Zamolodchikov criterion for the corresponding Pohlmeyer-reduced models, we are able to distinguish between integrable and non-integrable cases, in line with expectations from recent analytic and numerical studies. We conclude that Pohlmeyer reduction can provide a useful perspective on open-string non-integrability.

title: A Liouville theorem for the Hénon parabolic equation
authors: Yuxia Guo, Wenjun Wang, Tingfeng Yuan
abstract: We prove that every nonnegative classical entire solution of $u_t-Δu=|x|^αu^p$ in $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ is identically zero when $n\ge3$, $α\ge0$, and $1 < p < \frac{n+2+2α}{n-2}$. The same conclusion holds for weighted parabolic Gross--Pitaevskii systems with nonlinearities of degree $p=2r+1$ and constant coupling coefficients $β_{ij}=β_{ji}\ge0$ and $β_{ii}>0$. Both results include the unweighted case and require no boundedness, radial symmetry, spatial decay, finite-energy, or growth assumptions. The range is optimal for both problems: bounded nonzero nonnegative stationary solutions exist for $p\ge\frac{n+2+2α}{n-2}$.

title: A Copper-Inducible Yeast Biosensor with Bioluminescent Readout: Mathematical Modeling, Experimental Validation, and Photodetector Coupling for Molecular Communication in IoBNT
authors: Nikolaos Ntetsikas, Styliana Kyriakoudi, Ariel Klavaris, Antonis Kirmizis, Chrysostomos Chrysostomou, Ian F. Akyildiz, Marios Lestas
abstract: Engineered living biosensors constitute promising model organisms for bringing Molecular Communications (MC) closer to practical applications. However, challenges associated with their development and characterization have resulted in the relevant literature being limited in the MC domain, . In this paper, we contribute in this direction by leveraging engineered yeast as a basis to detect heavy metals such as copper. The biosensor's development is supported by a validated mathematical characterization and analysis for possible integration in an MC system. Different from the existing literature, mathematical representations of the major biological processes within the yeast copper detoxification pathway are integrated into a comprehensive framework that predicts the time evolution of the CUP1 gene, which is treated as the system output. In the engineered circuit, CUP1 was replaced with GFP, therefore making GFP fluorescence the final system output. Experimental analysis including mRNA transcript quantification and fluorometric measurements, validate the GFP reporting model to a satisfactory degree. This establishes the proposed model as a useful tool for virtual experimentation and the developed testbed as a suitable platform for further engineering of yeast-based copper sensors. The theoretical analysis is further extended by incorporating a self-sustained bioluminescent reporter for yeast, replacing GFP and enabling optical output without external light excitation. The optical response is coupled to a photodetector model, rendering the system suitable for integration into mobile monitoring devices such as Smart Pills. The presented characterization of the yeast receiver as a copper biosensor, constitutes the first step towards the development and characterization of a complete end-to-end MC based system for gut theranostics after coupling with suitable engineered probiotic senders.

title: Maximal defect $2$-blocks with dihedral defect groups up to splendid Morita equivalence
authors: Shigeo Koshitani, Caroline Lassueur, İpek Tuvay, Deniz Yılmaz
abstract: We classify, up to splendid Morita equivalence, all maximal defect blocks whose defect groups are dihedral \(2\)-groups of order at least \(8\). The classification holds for blocks over an algebraically closed field as well as for those over a suitable discrete valuation ring of characteristic zero. As a consequence, Puig's conjecture holds for this infinite family of blocks. Beyond the classification result itself, a central feature of the present work is the variety of methods required in its proof. Our arguments combine classical techniques of block theory with a broad range of tools and techniques that have emerged over the past twenty-five years. Amongst others these include in a crucial manner the Gorenstein-Walter classification of finite groups with dihedral Sylow \(2\)-subgroups, Linckelmann's glueing of local Morita equivalences to obtain a stable equivalence of Morita type, the modern versions of Fong's 1st and 2nd reduction theorems in terms of splendid and endo-permutation source Morita equivalences, the structure of the Dade group of endo-permutation modules, Boltje-Perepelitsky's extended theory of Brauer pairs for \(p\)-permutation modules, the fusion systems of the blocks involved, or the concrete knowledge of their decomposition matrices.

title: Strong Fused Performance Can Mask Branch Collapse in a Dual-View Heart-Sound Classifier: A Three-Part Diagnostic Protocol
authors: Safayet Khan, Hasan Zohirul Islam, Md. Tauhid Bin Iqbal
abstract: Fusion models are usually judged by their fused score, a practice that assumes that every branch has learned something useful. We show that this assumption can fail silently in dual-view heart-sound classification. In AudioFuse, which fuses a spectrogram transformer with a waveform CNN, the spectrogram branch is unused despite strong fused performance when both branches are trained from scratch. We introduce a three-part diagnostic for branch collapse: whether deleting a branch changes the fused score, whether a linear probe on its features beats an untrained copy of the same branch, and whether the branch can learn its view when trained alone. Deleting the branch has negligible effect, and probing its features shows little improvement over an identically initialised, untrained copy. Yet the same architecture trained alone exceeds 0.9 AUC, so its view is learnable, while the jointly trained model is near chance when it must rely on this branch. Update statistics and an initialisation experiment point to an early optimisation imbalance. Moving a strong artificial label cue from one input to the other can switch which branch the model relies on, even though the branch architectures stay the same. We observe branch collapse on PhysioNet, but the full diagnostic is not met on ICBHI or CirCor. Fused performance alone therefore cannot establish that every branch learned a meaningful representation, and we recommend reporting branch deletion and an untrained-control probe alongside it.

title: Fast Training-Free Low-Light Video Enhancement with a Frozen Image Diffusion Prior
authors: Hon Ming Yam, Chun Pong Lau
abstract: Pretrained image diffusion models can enhance low-light video without low-light training data and without retraining for a new camera. ZVRD, the only published training-free method for low-light video, is too slow to use: our implementation needs over a minute per $256 \times 256$ frame. We present a causal, training-free pipeline that adds two temporal components to a frozen MR. Illuminate image prior. Temporal input fusion recursively averages motion-compensated low-light frames before diffusion inversion. Late-start offset propagation runs the full sampling trajectory only on key frames. Each non-key frame inverts the low-noise part of its own trajectory and adds an enhancement offset warped from the latest key frame. At ZVRD's own resolution the pipeline is $261\times$ faster than ZVRD and scores better on all five metrics we report. On 13 held-out SDSD clips at $1280 \times 720$, it improves on framewise eight-step processing by 0.55 dB in PSNR and 0.034 in LPIPS and halves the warping error, in 10% less time. Measurements inside the model show why, and a linear-Gaussian model of inversion explains them. Fusion removes frame-to-frame noise before inversion amplifies it. A flow error perturbs the transported offset ten times less than it perturbs a transported state. The perceptual gain does not transfer to low resolution: at $346 \times 260$, LPIPS is worse by 0.028. At 0.65 frames per second, the pipeline is an offline method.

title: Randomization-Based Nonparanormal Adjusted Marginal Inference
authors: Leticia Wüthrich, Mark Baillie, Susanne Dandl
abstract: Adjusting for prognostic baseline covariates in the analysis of randomized controlled trials is recommended to increase the precision of treatment effect estimates. Such adjustment, however, introduces a complication known as noncollapsibility: for effect measures such as the log-odds or log-hazard ratio, the estimated treatment effect becomes conditional instead of marginal. Methods that target a marginal estimand even after covariate adjustment have been developed, but typically rely on population-based inference, which assumes patients are randomly sampled from some larger population, rarely true in practice. Such methods have been shown to inflate type I error, particularly in small samples or when many covariates are adjusted for. Inference based on randomization requires no such assumption, as it relies on the randomization scheme, which is known exactly, yielding a test that is exact even in finite samples. We present a randomization-based test for covariate-adjusted marginal treatment effects, built on nonparanormal adjusted marginal inference, applicable to continuous, binary, ordinal, and time-to-event outcomes. In simulation studies, this test controls type I error where the standard Wald test does not. Applied to 20 historical phase III time-to-event randomized trials, the covariate-adjusted estimator achieves precision gains comparable to an existing competitor method.

title: Online Inference for Dynamic Categorical Regression
authors: Lorenzo Rimella, Augusto Fasano, Giovanni Rebaudo
abstract: The multinomial probit is a widely used model for categorical data in many applications, especially in econometrics and the discrete-choice literature. The computational challenges encountered when fitting this model still motivate ongoing research from the frequentist and Bayesian viewpoints. We consider a dynamic formulation based on a state-space model, where at each time one observes a sample from a multinomial probit whose parameter evolves according to Markovian dynamics, thereby inducing dependence across time. We show that the filtering and predictive distributions of the latent parameter belong to the unified skew-normal family, developing an associated i.i.d.\ sampler to approximate quantities of interest via Monte Carlo. Motivated by the computational bottlenecks of the sampler encountered for larger sample sizes, we also develop approximate methods for online inference based on assumed density filtering and expectation propagation. This gives more scalable, yet accurate, algorithms for online inference about the latent state and prediction of future observations. Finally, we derive a novel expectation maximization procedure to learn from the data the covariance matrix underlying the latent-utility representation of the multinomial probit. We investigate the performance of the proposed methods on simulated data and on a real dataset of reservations from an online booking platform.

title: Path Abstraction for Markov Reward Models: An Isabelle Formalisation in a Free Monoid View
authors: Arnd Hartmanns, Robert Modderman
abstract: The classical definition of discrete-time Markov chains maps pairs of states to transition probabilities. An alternative, proposed in the context of path abstraction in probabilistic counterexample refinement, is to view them as a transition kernel on the free monoid on the state space, mapping paths directly to path probabilities. In this paper, we first extend the free monoid view and path abstraction algorithm to cumulative rewards on Markov reward models. We then use Isabelle/HOL to formalise Markov chains and reward models in this view, exploiting the discrete finite-prefix semantics to work with Isabelle's standard HOL-Analysis library. We mechanise the path abstraction algorithm and its key correctness properties of well-definedness and monotonic absorption, establishing the preservation of reachability probabilities and expected rewards. Proving the convergence of these quantities on relevant path sets is aided by our use of the lightweight free monoid semantics in place of the standard measure-theoretic one used in established Isabelle formalisations of Markov models. We obtain a verified abstract implementation of path abstraction in Isabelle/HOL, providing a foundation for refinement to efficient executable code and integration with probabilistic model checkers.

title: Right Labels, Wrong Reasons: Signed Feature Attribution for Multi-Label Explainability
authors: Kenton White
abstract: When a multi-label classifier assigns the right labels, it may do so for the wrong reasons. Diffuse feature combinations may vary across classifier families and lack a dominant feature. This paper proposes FLEX (Fisher LDA Explainer), a global surrogate that fits a single direct multi-label Fisher LDA over the full binary label matrix, producing signed feature attribution lists for each label in a single coherent coordinate system. Across the evaluated benchmarks and classifier families, FLEX reproduces the black box's predictions with consistently high fidelity. Pooling covariance across labels outperforms a per-label alternative on most datasets, with the advantage growing largest where labels are numerous and positive examples are scarce. FLEX's fidelity-complexity Pareto curve is monotonically increasing, giving practitioners a predictable path to higher-fidelity explanations as more features are used, and its in-sample fidelity matches or leads Binary Relevance alternatives once a modest feature budget is allowed. The magnitude of each discriminant weight vector bounds its label's separability, flagging labels that may be predicted correctly for the wrong reasons. The evaluated classifiers largely agree on which predictions to make, but reach those decisions through different feature subsets when no single feature dominates.

title: MM-ReportBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal Report Generation from Tables
authors: Teng Lin, Nan Tang
abstract: The ability to generate multimodal reports integrating fluent narratives with faithful visualizations from tabular data, has become a cornerstone capability for modern vision-language models in practical domains such as finance, healthcare, and policy making. However, existing benchmarks are limited by single-modality focus, simplistic metrics, novelty evaluation, and visualization quality. We address these limitations with MM-ReportBench, a multimodal report evaluation benchmark covering 386 tasks across 185 real-world tables. Each task is paired with an expert-curated reference report featuring standardized chapter structures and verifiable key insight points, constructed through a hybrid pipeline of multimodal reports generation based on Monte Carlo Tree Search and rigorous human quality control. For robust evaluation, we design a dual-judge evaluation framework: Text Judge Model assesses textual quality along structural completeness, grounded insight verification with numerical fact-checking against source tables, and novelty analysis that distinguishes genuine analytical discovery from trivial paraphrasing; Visualization Judge Model evaluates generated visualizations across data fidelity, expressiveness, aesthetics, and technical correctness. They also evaluate cross-modal consistency. Extensive experiments on 20 state-of-the-art models reveal critical weaknesses: even the strongest model achieves only 68.9 overall score, with numerical hallucination affecting 38.5% of reports and genuinely novel insights remaining rare. Our ablation studies further demonstrate that single-judge evaluation consistently inflates scores by 8-12 points compared to dual-judge assessment, confirming that rigorous and reliable benchmarking demands multi-faceted, complementary evaluation probes.

title: ATS: Anti-Aliased Triangle Splatting with Exact Per-Primitive Integrals
authors: Brent Zoomers, Joni Vanherck, Leander Winters, Jeroen Put, Lode Jorissen, Nick Michiels
abstract: Triangle Splatting represents scenes using semi-transparent triangles, but it evaluates each triangle at the pixel center and culls any triangle with an inradius smaller than one pixel. The former causes severe aliasing, while the latter culls most of the scene at lower resolutions. We show that the integral of the Triangle Splatting window over a pixel admits an exact closed-form solution. The angle bisectors split the triangle into three sub-triangles, in each of which the window is a power of the distance to one edge. Each piece therefore has a closed-form antiderivative, and Green's theorem reduces the integral and its gradients to one term per side of the sub-triangle clipped against the pixel. The integral over the whole triangle, which we show has a closed form, then allows conservative culling, removing only triangles that cannot meet the renderer's alpha cutoff at any pixel. This exact formulation anti-aliases existing models without retraining, exhibits less temporal aliasing than 2x2 supersampling, and enables multi-scale training, matching or outperforming supersampled training at reduced resolutions.

title: From Relevance to Utility: Rubric Alignment in Yuanbao Search
authors: Yu Lu, Lixin Zou, Yangqi Chen, Hui Xu, Qiaolin Xia, Hao Wang, Qianwen Ma, Reed Li, Shuang Zeng, Haijin Liang, Haibo Shi
abstract: Agentic search demands that a search engine move beyond per document relevance ranking to assemble document sets optimized for downstream LLM reasoning. Prior work addresses this either by improving individual pipeline stages in isolation or by applying RL based selection on top of relevance trained upstream modules, leaving the full stack unaligned to utility for reasoning. We propose rubric aligned search, a framework that unifies the traditional search pipeline under a single supervision surface. For each query, we derive a rubric from coarse to fine, specifying weighted positive criteria that the document set must satisfy and negative criteria that it must avoid. From this rubric we derive two training signals. First, a lightweight labeler distills rubric grounded judgments into per document utility labels, which supervise a contrastive dual encoder for retrieval and a multi task ranker trained with four rubric aligned scoring heads. Second, a rubric conditioned evaluator produces a set level reward that drives a dual branch RL selector, combining GRPO with best rollout distillation to resolve credit assignment in subset optimization. Deployed in Yuanbao Search, the pipeline improves end to end answer quality by 8.52% over the online production baseline.

title: Stability for a multi-frequency inverse source problem in diffusion-based tomography
authors: Dong Qiu, Xiang Xu, Ruiting Zhao, Yue Zhao
abstract: This paper is concerned with the inverse source problem for the time-harmonic diffusion equation arising in optical tomography. In inhomogeneous media, we establish a conditional logarithmic stability estimate by using multi-frequency boundary flux measurements. The proof combines a boundary observability inequality for the associated heat equation with quantitative analytic continuation. For constant coefficients, we further derive an increasing stability estimate with explicit dependence on the frequency bandwidth. In this case, the analysis employs complex polynomial interpolation of the Fourier-Laplace transform of the source. We also implement a multi-frequency Landweber iteration with a discrepancy-based stopping rule to reconstruct the sources. Numerical experiments show an overall improvement in reconstruction accuracy and resolution as the frequency bandwidth increases under the tested noise settings.

title: Burgers vectors from Voronoi topology
authors: Emanuel A. Lazar
abstract: Automated dislocation analysis is standard in atomistic simulations, yet current tools are limited to a handful of crystal structures. We introduce an algorithm without adjustable parameters, based on Voronoi topology, that identifies dislocations in a broad class of crystals. Each face shared by two cells that match the ideal crystal is taken as a step in it, and summing these steps around closed circuits of such cells yields exact Burgers vectors, without geometric templates. Tested on dislocations inserted into all 9,610 Materials Project structures whose Voronoi cells are stable with a wide margin, the algorithm finds every dislocation with its correct Burgers vector. In raw molecular-dynamics snapshots, including eleven dislocation types in $θ$-Al$_2$Cu and bcc iron up to its melting point, every Burgers vector it returns is correct, although near melting the dislocations merge into one cluster. Voronoi topology thus provides a natural language in which a crystal, its defects, and their Burgers vectors are all described.

title: Dual and Binary AGN at Cosmic Dawn: The need for a JWST Program to resolve the merger channel of Early Black Hole Growth
authors: Filippo Mannucci, Matteo Ceci, Norman A. Grogin, Anton M. Koekemoer, Muhammad A. Latif, Alessandro Marconi, Enikő Regős, Raffaella Schneider, Martina Scialpi, Giulia Tozzi, Alessandro Trinca, Giacomo Venturi, Maria Vittoria Zanchettin, Huanian Zhang
abstract: The discovery with JWST of accreting black holes (BHs) at z=4-9 in numbers far exceeding pre-JWST expectations, many of them overmassive relative to their hosts and linked to the enigmatic Little Red Dots (LRDs), raises the question of how early BHs form and grow. Hierarchical assembly predicts that galaxy mergers drive gas to galactic nuclei and bring BHs together, leaving a direct observational signature: dual AGN at tens of kpc separations and sub-kpc to few-kpc "duets" in post-merger galaxies, which are the progenitors of the low-frequency GW sources targeted by pulsar timing arrays and LISA. JWST has opened the window to study these systems at z>3. However, these early discoveries are very limited number and come from heterogeneous, largely serendipitous samples, so these systems can hardly be used for robust statistical studies. Within the Genesis initiative We propose a uniformly selected census of dual AGN and their hosts from cosmic noon to cosmic dawn, as a science case for the Genesis initiative. Our tiered strategy uses the survey imaging and spectroscopy for candidate selection at no extra cost, followed by NIRSpec IFU confirmation, multi-band NIRCam (and MIRI/ALMA) host characterisation, and multi-epoch revisits. Confirming and characterising about 100 pairs requires of order 1000 hr, well beyond the ceiling of standard TAC programs, and demands multi-cycle continuity. The census will deliver pair fractions as functions of redshift, separation and luminosity, BH masses and mass ratios, host properties and environments, and the empirical anchor needed to turn merger models into realistic LISA rate forecasts.

title: On representation-theoretic and homological properties of distance algebras of finite graphs
authors: Aaron Chan, Bohan Xing
abstract: Distance algebras were introduced by Asao and Ivanov to realize magnitude homology and cohomology as bigraded Tor and Ext groups. We study the representation-theoretic and homological properties of the distance algebra $Σ_G$ of a finite connected graph $G$. We characterize the graphs for which $Σ_G$ is representation-finite, multiserial, biserial, or self-injective by an explicit graph-theoretic classification. We also compute the finitistic, self-injective, and dominant dimensions for several natural families of graphs. For a finite modular lattice $L$, we consider the distance algebra $Σ_L$ associated to the Hasse graph of $L$, and show that $Σ_L$ is Auslander--Gorenstein precisely when $L$ is a finite direct product of chains. We also present a family of minimal Auslander--Gorenstein distance algebras, namely, those associated to punctured hypercubes, whose finitistic (equivalently, self-injective; equivalently, dominant) dimension can be arbitrarily large.

title: Fine-Grained Japanese Clinical Named Entity Recognition: A Controlled Comparison of BERT and Open-Weight Large Language Models
authors: Feng Han, Ayako Yagahara, Kenji Hirata, Atsushi Yoshida, Kohsuke Kudo
abstract: Background: Generative large language models (LLMs) offer an alternative to encoder-based clinical named entity recognition (NER), but their performance on fine-grained Japanese extraction tasks and sensitivity to generation settings remain uncertain. Methods: We compared two fine-tuned BERT-CRF baselines with nine open-weight LLMs on iCorpus, which defines 113 entity categories. The evaluation used 433 sentences from 36 test documents; 1,672 sentences were used for training. LLMs were evaluated using zero-shot prompting with and without JSON Schema constraints and three-seed QLoRA fine-tuning. Fine-tuned models were assessed under different output-token limits, including 900 and larger model-specific limits of 2,600 or 4,096 tokens. Performance was measured using sentence-level label-surface matching with relaxed and exact-surface F1. Results: The highest zero-shot relaxed F1 was 0.337, compared with 0.836-0.841 for the BERT baselines. At the larger output limits, all eight fine-tuned LLMs with at least 13B total parameters exceeded both BERT baselines (relaxed F1, 0.882-0.914; exact-surface F1, 0.840-0.880). Across three-seed means, increasing the output limit improved relaxed F1 by 0.052-0.085, alongside higher recall and fewer length-limited outputs. JSON Schema constraints changed relaxed F1 by -0.014 to +0.008 among seven models outside the two reasoning-oriented configurations, while medical-general model pairs showed no consistent advantage for medical specialization. Conclusions: On this historical Japanese case-report benchmark, task-specific fine-tuning combined with adequate generation capacity was associated with stronger LLM extraction performance. Output-token limits materially affected comparisons with BERT, whereas enforcing output structure alone did not overcome low zero-shot accuracy.

title: Settling the Time and Structural Complexity of Bertrand Networks
authors: MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi, Suho Shin
abstract: In the seminal Bertrand network game introduced by Babaioff et al. (2013), each seller posts a single price to captive buyers and to the markets it shares with neighboring sellers, where sellers cannot price discriminate across the markets. Although the existence of equilibria and polynomial-time algorithms to compute them in trees (Babaioff et al. (2013)) have been known, it has been a major open problem whether there exist efficient algorithms to compute them for general graphs. In this paper, we resolve this open question negatively by proving that computing any constant-error approximate Nash equilibrium in a Bertrand network is $\PPAD$-complete. This hardness holds even on sparse bipartite graphs of maximum degree five with constant integer market weights. Complementing our hardness result, we design an efficient polynomial-time approximation scheme (EPTAS) when both the maximum degree and the number of sellers with captive buyers are bounded. Beyond time complexity, since exact equilibria require randomizing prices over continuous intervals, another fundamental question left open by Babaioff et al. (2013) is whether an exact equilibrium can always be represented with a finite number of price intervals, \ie whether its structural complexity is finite. We resolve this question affirmatively by proving that every achievable equilibrium revenue profile can be realized by an equilibrium with structural complexity $O(2^n)$, which leads to an exact algorithm running in doubly exponential time. We further show that this bound is tight: there exist instances for which the unique equilibrium realizing target revenue profiles has structural complexity $Ω(2^n)$.

title: Joint-ID: Transformer-based Joint Image Enhancement and Depth Estimation for Underwater Environments
authors: Geonmo Yang, Gilhwan Kang, Juhui Lee, Younggun Cho
abstract: Underwater imaging is a challenging task due to factors such as scattering, absorption, and turbulence, which degrade image quality and limit visibility. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for enhancing underwater images that leverages the benefits of joint learning for simultaneous image enhancement and depth estimation. We introduce Joint-ID, a transformer-based neural network that can obtain high-perceptual image quality and depth information from raw underwater images. Our approach formulates a multi-modal objective function that addresses invalid depth, lack of sharpness, and image degradation based on color and local texture. We design an end-to-end training pipeline that enables joint restoration and depth estimation in a shared hierarchical feature space. Additionally, we propose a synthetic dataset with various distortions and scene depths for multi-task learning. We evaluate Joint-ID on synthetic and standard datasets, as well as real underwater images with diverse spectra and harsh turbidity, demonstrating its effectiveness for underwater image enhancement and depth estimation. Furthermore, we demonstrate the ability of Joint-ID to perform feature matching and saliency detection for visually guided underwater robots. Our proposed method has the potential to improve the visual perception of underwater environments and benefit applications such as oceanography and underwater robotics. Supplements are available at: https://sites.google.com/view/joint-id/home

title: Haptic Probing for Subsurface-Aware Force Distribution on Layered Soft Tissue
authors: Lei Shi, Xiaoyu Wang, Cheng Zhou, Yongjian Liu, Jing Wang, Dongsheng Zhang, Yonghui Zhu, Xiong Li
abstract: Force-regulated contact with layered soft tissue fails most often where the subsurface composition changes: controllers infer the substrate from the loading signal alone, so the estimate guiding them lags the change---more acutely, we argue, over compliant than over bone-backed tissue. We remove that lag with a separate haptic channel. Under a light preload, a brief low-amplitude excitation lets the local dynamic admittance discriminate muscle from bone-backed tissue relative to a per-subject baseline, before task force is applied---active haptic sensing used to commit a control decision rather than to characterise tissue. A force- and tactile-driven distribution law then consumes that regime throughout execution: an instantaneous allocation equalises pressure across the engaged fingertips, while the regime sets the admissible pressure and hence the area the hand must recruit to deliver the target force---making patch area a controlled variable rather than a by-product. Probing, switches and recruitment are priced in a partitioned passivity budget, so safety monitoring cannot suppress the probe and a refused recruitment forfeits force tracking rather than the pressure bound. We report force tracking and pressure uniformity over curved, migrating contact on three human subjects, with regime labels from anatomical landmarks.

title: Stable recurrences of the super-transition array formalism from marked generating functions
authors: Daniel Aberg, Brian G. Wilson, Jean-Christophe Pain
abstract: The conventional evaluation of super-transition-array (STA) mean energies and variances uses partition recurrences with alternating terms that can lose numerical accuracy. Here we apply a marked-generating-function approach to derive coupled coefficient recurrence relations that avoid these sums and directly accumulate fixed-occupation partition functions and arbitrary-order moments of the configuration-average (centroid) transition energies. Unlike explicit expansions into products of subshell occupations, the resulting recurrences require only one coefficient numerator per moment order. The same approach provides recurrences for polynomial occupation-number averages, which can be contracted to obtain the contributions of individual configurations to the STA variance and the Boltzmann energy correction entering the partition function. These contractions avoid the explicit evaluation of individual occupation-product averages and reduce the number of auxiliary quantities required. Numerical examples demonstrate agreement with direct configuration enumeration, including regimes where the alternating Bar--Shalom recurrences lose accuracy. Complementary hole-counting recurrences are also derived for all quantities, starting from a full supershell.

title: Symmetry-selected entanglement death at Floquet resonances of parametrically coupled qubits
authors: Kamran Akbari, Stephen Hughes
abstract: Periodic modulation of a qubit--qubit coupling is a standard way to engineer quantum interactions, but a strong modulation also reorganizes the transitions through which the qubits dissipate into a comb of Floquet channels. We study two identical, strongly coupled qubits whose transverse coupling is modulated anharmonically, as by a nonlinear coupler, with each qubit damped by its own reservoir. The modulation raises the ground-state concurrence of the cycle-averaged Hamiltonian from 0.45 to above 0.8, yet the steady-state concurrence stays close to its undriven value except at Floquet resonances selected by symmetry. There it undergoes entanglement death, vanishing at all times in the drive cycle over a finite range of modulation depths. Parity and exchange symmetry split the Floquet spectrum into an even sector, whose branches anticross at multiphoton resonances, and an exactly solvable odd sector, whose branches cross. Every dissipative channel connects the two sectors, so only the even anticrossings cause entanglement death, provided their gap exceeds the damping rate, whereas the nearby odd crossings leave the concurrence unchanged.
